title: Finite occupied-and-empty conditioning preserves projection Pfaffian point processes under the stated doubled-space regularity condition
author: Shinji Koshida
work: Pfaffian Point Processes from Free Fermion Algebras: Perfectness and Conditional Measures
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 008, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.008; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof reduces finite mixed conditioning to single-point steps while tracking the projection regularity and the doubled-space involution. It derives two successive projection reductions, computes the conditioned Pfaffian correlations, and identifies the resulting kernel with the projection onto the explicitly modified subspace. This simultaneously verifies the probability-law and Hilbert-space descriptions, rather than just applying a finite Pfaffian Schur complement.

source_check.note: Complete author Theorem1.17 proof in Section4, including its new projection/subspace reduction and correlation identification, is read and supplied. X is countable, K=l2(X) direct-sum l2(X) with the conjugate-swap involution Gamma, P belongs to Gr(K,Gamma), and the finite occupied/empty subsets are disjoint with P K intersect(K_plus occupied direct-sum K_minus empty)={0}. The conditional law on the deleted configuration space is exactly the PfPP corresponding to the orthogonal projection onto (P K plus K_plus occupied plus K_minus empty) intersect the remaining doubled space. The local regularity/decomposition lemmas state the finite reductions explicitly; symmetric routine cases are identified as such by the source. The full existence proof1.3/2.2 is included; prior Araki quasi-free states and the standard finite-dimensional projection reduction are author-cited background. No Schur-perfectness, shifted-Schur or continuous-space extension is separately counted. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.
